newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks drift down in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks drift down in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks dipped lower at the start of trading on Wednesday morning due to investor hesitation at the psychological resistance level of 12,000, brokers said.
"We are still confident on the market, but there is a good bit of caution at this level," said Ronald Lam, chief dealer at Dao Heng Securities.
The Hang Seng Index eased 20.53 points to 11,900.69 after 30 minutes of active trade. Turnover was HK$906 million in early trading.
"The finance sector is holding up the market," said Lam.
"All other sectors are undergoing profit-taking," Lam said.
Peter Lui in institutional sales at NAVA SC Securities said he was not surprised to see the market undergo a short-term correction following the strong gains.
"We could see a 100-point dip before the market returns to its uptrend," Lui said, adding that he was still very positive on the market in both the short and medium term.
The Hang Seng will test its record high by the end of the year, he said. The index hit an all-time intraday peak of 12,599 in January 1994.
In the finance sector, HSBC was holding steady at HK$143.50 after earlier nudging up to HK$144.00. Hang Seng Bank, which hit a record high of HK$83.25 on Tuesday, drifted down HK$0.50 to HK$82.75.
Property stocks faced the greatest selling pressure. Sun Hung Properties which will report earnings for the year ended June 30 on Wednesday, dropped HK$1.00 to HK$81.50.
Henderson Land lost HK$0.50 to HK$65.75 and Cheung Kong declined HK$0.50 to HK$59.25. The share briefly touched a new high of HK$60.25 before succumbing to profit-taking.

Utilities also came in for some profit-taking. Hong Kong Telecom was unchanged at the HK$14.15, after dipping to HK$14.10. The share, a laggard in the first stages of the market's recent rally, had outperformed during the past two to three days.
"The share still has good upside," said NAVA's Lui. "It is not expensive at all when compared to other regional telecoms plays like Singapore Telecom."
Consolidated Electric Power Asia (CEPA)and Hopewell were among the most active shares. CEPA eased HK$0.30 to HK$15.75 and its parent Hopewell held steady at HK$4.525.
CEPA had risen recently after Hopewell said it was in talks to sell some or all of its shares in CEPA.
